ops.title: Release tags must be annotated AND GPG-signed by the trusted release key

ops.body:
The Release workflow's first job, `verify-tag-on-main` (the shared `yasyf/homebrew-tap/.github/actions/verify-tag-on-main` action), enforces **three** properties on the pushed tag. Every downstream job — helper app, pure CLI matrix, smoke, publish release, bump-formula — depends on that gate, so a violation means nothing builds and no release is created.

Each failed attempt permanently burns a version number: a repository ruleset blocks tag deletion on origin (`! [remote rejected] vX.Y.Z (push declined due to repository rule violations)`), so a bad tag can never be removed or replaced. On 2026-07-25 this cost v0.47.7 (lightweight) and v0.47.8 (unsigned) before v0.47.9 landed — all three on the same commit ba1eaa9.

**The three requirements:**

1. **Annotated**, not lightweight. `git tag vX.Y.Z <commit>` creates a lightweight ref and fails with `remote ref is not an annotated tag object (type='commit'); lightweight tags are forbidden`.
2. **GPG-signed by the trusted release key** `F3299DE3FE0F6C3CF2B66BFBF7ECDD88A700D73A` (the action pins this as `TRUSTED_RELEASE_FINGERPRINT`). An annotated but unsigned tag fails with `GitHub did not verify the tag signature (reason='unsigned')`. Note git's configured `user.signingkey` in this repo is a *different* key, so `-u <fingerprint>` must be explicit.
3. **Tagger identity `Yasyf Mohamedali <yasyfm@gmail.com>`** — the UID on the trusted key. The repo's `user.email` is `yasyf@poetic.com`, which would not match the key UID, so GitHub would not verify the signature. Override per-command; don't mutate git config.

**The command that works:**

```
GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="Yasyf Mohamedali" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="yasyfm@gmail.com" \
  git tag -s -u F3299DE3FE0F6C3CF2B66BFBF7ECDD88A700D73A -m "vX.Y.Z

<one-line summary>" vX.Y.Z <commit-on-main>
```

**Verify all of it locally before pushing** — this is the entire difference between a release and a permanently wasted version number:

```
git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z                     # must print "tag"
git cat-file tag vX.Y.Z | grep ^tagger     # must be yasyfm@gmail.com
git verify-tag vX.Y.Z                      # must show the F3299... fingerprint
```

After pushing, confirm GitHub's own view before assuming success:

```
gh api repos/yasyf/cc-notes/git/tags/$(git rev-parse vX.Y.Z) \
  --jq '"verified=\(.verification.verified) reason=\(.verification.reason)"'
# want: verified=true reason=valid
```

Comparing against the previous successful tag (`git cat-file tag <last-release>`) is the fastest way to spot a drifted property. This is separate from the AGENTS.md rule about never re-tagging a *published* stable version; here nothing published, but the ruleset makes tags immutable regardless.

ops.when: Before cutting a cc-notes release tag, or when a Release workflow run fails at verify-tag-on-main
